claims.claim: R2 registered prediction 1, verbatim (REVERSE-ACTUALIZE.md R2 + spec/primitives-v2.md B.2): rate over a constant stream is exactly 0 within 1e-9 for every window; with injected jitter ±ε/2 it stays 0 (deadband works); with jitter ±2ε it oscillates — naming the honest sensitivity boundary instead of hiding it. Instrument: src/calculus.js rate = backward difference over the last w samples, deadband law verbatim spec B.2 '|ΔV| < deadband → 0 exactly', deadband ε = 0.04 (the isDegenerate spread<0.04 law from quilt-storefront src/vector.js). Pre-declared deterministic streams, no post-hoc choice: constant stream V_i = 0.5 for i = 1..64, windows w ∈ {1,2,4}; jitter sequence J1 (the ±ε/2 case): per-sample jitter s_i·ε/2 with s alternating 0,+1 (so consecutive-sample |ΔV| = ε/2 < ε — killed); jitter sequence J2 (the ±2ε case): per-sample jitter s_i·2ε with s alternating −2,+2 (so consecutive-sample |ΔV| = 4ε — survives). Metric: metrics.p1_deadband_holds == 1, conjunct of (metrics.p1_constant_zero == 1 AND metrics.p1_half_jitter_zero == 1 AND metrics.p1_double_jitter_oscillates == 1).
claims.refusal: Any constant-stream window reading with |rate| > 1e-9 → FAIL. Any nonzero rate under J1 → the deadband law fails at its registered setting → FAIL. ALL windows zero under J2 → the deadband hides real dynamics (no honest sensitivity boundary) → FAIL. Numeric pitfalls are the test's to avoid, not the claim's to soften: the boundary is |ΔV| < ε strictly, and J1/J2 were fixed pre-run so the strict inequality is exercised on both sides.
